population.span: This multicenter, randomized clinical trial enrolled 1105 patients with heart failure (defined as having a left ventricular ejection fraction of ≤45%) and iron deficiency (serum ferritin level <100 ng/mL; or if transferrin saturation was <20%, a serum ferritin level between 100 ng/mL and 299 ng/mL)

endpoint.span: The second primary outcome (total heart failure hospitalizations)

estimate.span: The second primary outcome (total heart failure hospitalizations) occurred 264 times in the ferric carboxymaltose group vs 320 times in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.60-1.06]

ci.span: The second primary outcome (total heart failure hospitalizations) occurred 264 times in the ferric carboxymaltose group vs 320 times in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.60-1.06]

treatment_strategy.span: Administration of ferric carboxymaltose (n = 558) initially given at an intravenous dose of up to 2000 mg that was followed by 500 mg every 4 months (unless stopping criteria were met) vs a saline placebo (n = 547).

follow_up.span: The median follow-up was 16.6 months (IQR, 7.9-29.9 months).
